definition.intro: A chain where the end of the chain can turn the start back down.

definition.mechanism: A signed cycle in the relationship graph: one edge carries an inhibitory effect from a downstream node back to an upstream source, so continued output reduces its own trigger.

explanations.question: Why does the Source structure act on the Intermediary structure?

answer.intro: Because the invented episode makes the Source release Alpha, and Alpha reaches the Intermediary.
answer.standard: The authored trigger causes Alpha release. Alpha is carried to the Intermediary structure, which responds by releasing Beta.
answer.mechanism: In the fixture, the trigger event sets the Source highlight and marks Alpha increasing. The edge is causal and its route is schematic, so the pulse shown on it is presentation emphasis and not a measured transit.

explanations.question: How does Alpha reach the Intermediary structure?

answer.intro: It is carried along an invented route drawn as a schematic line.
answer.standard: The fixture models transport as a schematic circulation route between two anchors.
answer.mechanism: This is the deepest explanation in this lesson. The route stores anchor identifiers and control points only; it is not a depiction of any vessel.

explanations.question: Why is this edge drawn with an arrowhead rather than a bar?

answer.intro: Because in this invented system Alpha increases the Intermediary's activity.
answer.standard: An arrowhead with the word stimulates marks an increasing effect; a terminal bar with the word inhibits marks a decreasing one.
answer.mechanism: This is the deepest explanation in this lesson. Sign belongs to the relationship record, so the same sign appears in the scene, the diagram and the transcript.

explanations.question: Why does the Intermediary structure act on the Peripheral structure?

answer.intro: Because Beta travels onward and makes the Peripheral structure release Gamma.
answer.standard: Beta is released in response to Alpha and acts on the Peripheral structure, whose output is Gamma.
answer.mechanism: The fixture authors this as a second causal edge so that a chain of at least three nodes can be tested end to end.

explanations.question: Why does Gamma reduce Alpha instead of increasing it?

answer.intro: Because this invented loop turns itself down once the output has been produced.
answer.standard: Gamma acts back on the Source structure with an inhibitory effect, so continued output reduces the signal that started it.
answer.mechanism: The feedback flag and the inhibitory effect both live on the relationship record. The renderer draws a terminal bar and the word inhibits; it does not infer a sign by drawing a circle.

explanations.question: Does the lesson say how long this takes?

answer.intro: No. It only says which response is described as arriving later.
answer.standard: The lesson position scrubber measures presentation time. Biological timing labels sit beside the tracks and say only earlier or later.
answer.mechanism: This is the deepest explanation in this lesson. No conversion exists between presentation milliseconds and any real duration, and none can be derived from this fixture.

explanations.question: Why does a second structure light up at the same time?

answer.intro: Because a second invented track responds during the same episode.
answer.standard: Two authored tracks share one presentation cursor, so their events are shown together rather than as two separate players.
answer.mechanism: Both tracks write into one semantic frame. Two commands writing the same property at the same instant fail validation, so the picture cannot depend on render order.

explanations.question: Why is this connector dashed and without an arrow?

answer.intro: Because it shows that two things go together, not that one causes the other.
answer.standard: Association is drawn as a non-directional dashed connector and never carries a travelling pulse.
answer.mechanism: An associative edge may only use the associated-with effect, so it cannot drive a causal animation even if an author tries.

timelines.label: Abstract exercise: an invented signalling loop

description.intro: A made-up system with three signals, used to practise reading a chain and its feedback.
description.standard: An abstract exercise using invented structures and signals. It practises the shape of a signalling chain and its regulation without depicting any real anatomy.
description.mechanism: Engineering fixture and abstract exercise. It exercises sequence, parallel tracks, an inhibitory feedback edge and two checkpoint predictions, using entities that deliberately do not exist.

timingBands.note: Ordering only. This lesson claims no duration of any kind.

caption.standard: The parallel track starts at rest and responds later during the same episode.
caption.mechanism: Every track carries an initial step at zero so the projection has a defined state for each track at any cursor.

steps.label: Alpha travels to the Intermediary structure

caption.intro: Alpha moves along the drawn route towards the middle structure.
caption.standard: Alpha is communicated along a schematic route to the Intermediary structure. The route legend explains what the line does and does not mean.
caption.mechanism: The route becomes visible and the Alpha trend is set to increasing. Pulse motion along the route is presentation emphasis only.

caption.intro: The middle structure receives Alpha and responds.
caption.standard: The Intermediary structure is marked as a target and releases Beta in response to Alpha.
caption.mechanism: Target highlight command. The step names the relationship so the semantic state is readable without watching the animation.

caption.intro: At the same time, the second structure responds too.
caption.standard: The parallel track reaches its own target state during the same episode, independently of the main chain.
caption.mechanism: Two tracks write different properties at the same timestamp. Writing the same property at one timestamp would fail validation.

caption.intro: The end of the chain sends out Gamma.
caption.standard: Beta stimulates the Peripheral structure, whose output signal Gamma begins to increase.
caption.mechanism: The forward route becomes visible and the Gamma trend is set to increasing. Trends are ordinal teaching cues with no units.

caption.intro: Gamma turns the start of the chain back down.
caption.standard: The regulating edge becomes visible: Gamma inhibits further Alpha release, and the Alpha trend turns to decreasing.
caption.mechanism: Inhibitory feedback edge with a terminal bar and the word inhibits. Sign and feedback come from the relationship record, not from the drawn shape.

limitations.intro: Everything here is invented. It teaches the shape of a loop, not a real body.

summary.intro: A made-up signal went down a chain, produced an output, and that output turned the start back down.

summary.mechanism: Sequence with one regulating edge: two forward causal edges on a schematic route, one parallel descriptive track, and an inhibitory feedback edge that changes an ordinal trend rather than any quantity.

summary.mechanism: The scenario demonstrates parallel timing on one shared cursor: per-track steps, persistent highlights with an authored shared-organ schedule, and trends that change only at authored events. Real stress biology is a reviewed lesson, not this fixture.

comparisons.title: Alpha and Beta in the invented loop

explanation.intro: Two invented signals from the same made-up episode: Alpha starts the chain and Beta carries it one step further.
explanation.standard: Alpha and Beta are distinct signals with distinct routes in the invented episode. Alpha leaves the source structure; Beta is released by the middle structure after Alpha arrives. Comparing them shows how a chain divides one story into steps.
explanation.mechanism: The fixture authors Alpha as the source-structure output and Beta as the middle-structure output, each with its own route and target. Their comparison demonstrates aligned authored dimensions; nothing here implies the two signals are interchangeable or that either models a real hormone.
